3 Tcl Commands 
 3.3 Command Description 
 
SUG1220-2.1E 
36(72) 
 
Usage 
Name 
Description  
<0|1> 
0: Physical constraint warnings will not be elevated to 
errors. 
1: Physical constraint warnings will be elevated to errors. 
Type 
Project 
Description  
Elevates physical constraint warnings to errors when running Place & 
Route. The default value is 1. 
Parameter 
<0|1>: Disable or enable promoting physical constraint warnings to 
errors during Place & Route. 
Example 
set_option -cst_warn_to_error 1 
-rpt_auto_place_io_info  
Reports auto-placed IO location information. 
Syntax 
-rpt_auto_place_io_info <0|1> 
Usage 
Name 
Description  
<0|1> 
0: Auto-placed IO location information will not be reported. 
1: Auto-placed IO location information will be reported. 
Type 
Project 
Description  
Reports auto-placed IO location information when running Place & 
Route. The default value is 0. 
Parameter 
<0|1>: Disable or enable reporting the IO location information of 
automatically placed pins. 
Example 
set_option -cst_warn_to_error 1 
-place_option  
Placement algorithm option. 
Syntax 
-place_option <0|1|2|3|4>

3 Tcl Commands 
 3.3 Command Description 
 
SUG1220-2.1E 
37(72) 
 
Usage 
Name 
Description  
<0|1|2|3|4> 
0: Default placement algorithm, with compilation speed 
prioritized. 
1: Routability prioritized. 
2: Timing prioritized. 
3: Attempts to achieve a better placement result. 
4: Attempts to achieve a better placement result. 
Type 
Project 
Description  
Placement algorithm option. The default value is 0. 
Parameter 
<0|1|2|3|4>: Placement algorithm option. 
Example 
set_option -place_option 1 
-route_option  
Routing algorithm option. 
Syntax 
-route_option <0|1|2> 
Usage 
Name 
Description  
<0|1|2> 
0: Uses the default routing algorithm. 
1: Sacrifices compilation speed to attempt to achieve a 
better routing result. 
2: Improves routing speed. 
Type 
Project 
Description  
Routing algorithm option. The default value is 0. 
Parameter 
<0|1|2>: Routing algorithm option. 
Example 
set_option -route_option 1 
-ireg_in_iob   
Places registers connected to input buffers into the IOB. 
Syntax 
-ireg_in_iob <0|1>
